name: Step 1 — Content-addressed objects
expected_behavior: # Step 1 — Content-addressed objects  Implement `blobstore.objects` according to the local architecture contract. Provide `ObjectStore(root)`, `put_bytes`, `put_stream`, `get`, `exists`, `verify`, and `iter_ids`, plus explicit corruption and invalid-ID errors. Use SHA-256 sharded paths and atomic durable publication. Existing corrupt content must be reported, never silently replaced. Reads and verification are read-only. Do not implement later subsystems.

name: Step 2 — Named manifests
expected_behavior: # Step 2 — Named manifests  Keep Step 1 working and implement `blobstore.manifests`. Provide `ManifestStore(root, objects)` with `create`, `get`, `delete`, `iter_names`, and `referenced_ids`. Validate safe hierarchical names, object IDs, existence, and digest integrity before publishing canonical JSON atomically. Duplicate identical creation is idempotent; conflicting replacement is rejected.

name: Step 3 — Multipart uploads
expected_behavior: # Step 3 — Multipart uploads  Keep earlier steps working and implement `blobstore.uploads`. Upload sessions have immutable targets, numbered parts, per-part SHA-256, durable metadata, and idempotent retries. `complete(upload_id, part_count)` must require contiguous parts, concatenate without loading the entire upload twice, publish the final object and target manifest, and make completion retries return the same result.

name: Step 4 — Replication audit and repair
expected_behavior: # Step 4 — Replication audit and repair  Keep Steps 1–3 working and implement `blobstore.replicas`. A `ReplicaSet` replicates verified objects, audits healthy/missing/corrupt states deterministically, quarantines corrupt destination files, and repairs only from a healthy source. Repair must verify the destination and must not mutate the primary or an already healthy replica.

name: Step 5 — Safe garbage collection
expected_behavior: # Step 5 — Safe garbage collection  Keep the full system working and implement `blobstore.gc`. Compute reachability from manifests and incomplete upload parts. `plan()` returns sorted candidates and a state fingerprint; `apply(plan)` rejects stale plans and quarantines candidates before deletion. `audit()` and dry-run planning are deterministic and read-only. Never delete a reachable object.
